newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin urges restraint in Belarus crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin urges restraint in Belarus crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin urged both sides in the Belarus crisis on Tuesday to show restraint, saying this was a precondition for further integration between the two Slav states.
"President Boris Yeltsin considers civic accord and prevention of violence an absolute priority," Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing.
"He expects both sides to show restraint and adopt a balanced approach, believing that this a key condition for a success in Russian-Belarussian integration."

Yeltsin sent Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to negotiate a compromise between hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and his parliamentary opponents over a referendum aimed at boosting Lukashenko's powers.
But a deal signed last Friday, hailed by Yeltsin as a huge success of Russian diplomacy, collapsed in less than 24 hours and Lukashenko pressed on with the referendum despite international criticism.
He announced an overwhelming victory in the poll on Monday which allows him to dissolve parliament and call elections if the legislature resists his actions.
Parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky dismissed the vote as a "farce" and the constitutional court was due to meet to consider a possibility of impeaching Lukashenko.

Moscow favours Lukashenko's quest for closer ties with Russia but fears his autocratic style and lack of free-market economic reforms could prove a burden in the two-state union agreed by Yeltsin and the Belarus president last April.
